memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Jacob sent word to Rachel and Leah to come out to the fields where his flocks were. He said to them, 'I see that your father's attitude toward me is not what it was before, but the God of my father has been with me. You know that I've worked for your father with all my strength, yet your father has cheated me by changing my wages ten times. However, God has not allowed him to harm me. If he said, "The speckled ones will be your wages," then all the flocks gave birth to speckled young; and if he said, "The streaked ones will be your wages," then all the flocks bore streaked young. So God has taken away your father's livestock and has given them to me.'" - Gen 31:4-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob gathers his wives and tells them plainly what these years have been like. Laban had "cheated me by changing my wages ten times" — every time an arrangement started to favour Jacob, Laban shifted the terms. Twenty years of this would wear down anyone. Yet running through Jacob's account is a steady refrain: "the God of my father has been with me... God has not allowed him to harm me... God has taken away your father's livestock and has given them to me."

Here Jacob names the real source of his prosperity. It was not his peeled branches or his own cleverness — it was God. Whatever schemes Laban tried, and whatever methods Jacob attempted, in the end it was the Lord who protected Jacob and provided for him. God quietly overruled every unfair twist for Jacob's good.

This is a great comfort when we are treated unfairly. We may not be able to stop the "wage-changers" in our lives — the people who cheat, undercut, or take advantage of us. But God can. He is able to protect His people and provide for them despite the schemes of others. No injustice done to us is outside His reach.

If you are being dealt with unfairly, entrust it to God. He sees, He is with you, and He can bring good even out of others' wrongs (Rom 8:28).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I credit God, or my own efforts, for the good in my life?
2. Where am I facing unfair treatment I cannot control?
3. Can I trust God to protect and provide despite others' schemes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You overrule even the unfair schemes of others for the good of Your people. Help me to trust You as my protector and provider, and to give You the credit for every good thing. Amen.
